Azalea: A small-flower print with a name every golfer recognises from the second week of April. Quiet on the shirt, less so in what it is referring to.
Gold Dust: White, with gold flecked through it and a gold collar to finish. The one people notice from two fairways away without being able to say why.
Shadow: Charcoal on black, mottled like the light under trees. Dark enough for a tucked shirt at dinner, patterned enough that it is not a plain black polo.
Signature Black: No print at all. Black, with the clover and the wordmark in gold on the chest, for the days you want the clubs doing the talking.
Contour: Contour lines running across white, the same map that sits behind the numbers on this site. Tonal, so you only see it up close.
Marble: Gold and teal veining across white, like a cracked marble slab. The loudest thing we make, and it still passes at a private club.
Gold Carnation: Carnations in white on gold, with a gold collar. There is no version of this one that blends in, which is the point.
Frost: A frosted grey break across white. Tonal and cool, and the one to pick if you want pattern without colour.
Cruiser: Rows of little carts on sage green. You will be asked what is on your shirt, and you will enjoy answering.
Nightshade: White line flowers on black with a white collar and placket. The sharpest contrast in the rack, and the one that photographs best.
Swirl: A tonal swirl through white, no buttons, nothing at your throat. The blade collar version of a shirt you can wear anywhere.
Spot: The quietest one we make. Off-white with a faint speckle, blade collar, and no logo doing anything loud.
Blackout: Black on black, mottled, with a blade collar. If you want Lucky in the bag and nothing announcing it on the shirt, this is it.
